# Refuted claims and their evidence


- ❌ **[CRITICAL] The stated ΔG magnitudes are at or beyond the empirical ceiling for non-covalent binding: 6 of 25 exceed biotin–streptavidin, presented as routine output for 28–47-residue de novo peptides — Taken at face value (which is what the dashboard tile at index.html:74-75 and the leaderboard ΔG column at app.js:885 invite the reader to do), the stated free energies correspond to: -18.2 → 46 fM, -18.4 → 33 fM, -18.7 → 20 fM, -18.9 → 14 fM, -19.1 → 10 fM, -19.5 → 5.1 fM. Biotin–streptavidin, the canonical tightest non-covalent biological interaction, has Kd ≈ 4e-14 M → ΔG° = -18.28 kcal/mol (experimental value widely quoted as ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol). Six of the 25 candidates are therefore claimed to bind more tightly than biotin–streptavidin, and the flagship BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 (app.js:290) at -19.5 kcal/mol is claimed to be ~8-fold tighter than biotin–streptavidin. The remaining 19 sit between -15.2 and -17.8, i.e. 7 pM to 90 fM — still tighter than essentially any reported de novo designed peptide. For calibration, the best affinity-matured de novo mini-protein binders from state-of-the-art structure-based design reach roughly 20 pM to 10 nM (Cao et al., Nature 2022), i.e. ΔG° of -14.6 to -10.9 kcal/mol; unoptimized first-round designs are typically µM–nM. There is no ligand-efficiency argument that rescues these: -19.5 kcal/mol over the ~295 heavy atoms of a 39-mer is LE ≈ 0.066 kcal/mol per heavy atom, which is not itself anomalous, but the total is, because the interface a 28–47-residue linear peptide can bury is small and largely unpreorganized (these are flexible chains, several with unpaired cysteines and GGGGS linkers, so a large conformational-entropy penalty applies before any interface term is counted). The claimed affinities are also asserted uniformly across six unrelated target classes (RTK ectodomains, an AChE gorge, a Kelch β-propeller, a Frizzled CRD, a pentameric LGIC ECD, a membrane transporter), which is itself implausible — achievable affinity is strongly target- and epitope-dependent. Consequence: Femtomolar affinity is effectively irreversible on any biological timescale; a compound with Kd = 5 fM would not dissociate from its target over the lifetime of the cell, which contradicts the platform's own claim of 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2%' and reversible allosteric tuning (README.md:100-102). It also makes the safety narrative incoherent: at 5 fM the drug would be quantitatively bound to every copy of the target at concentrations far below one molecule per cell (one molecule in a 1 pL cell is ~1.7 nM). Any reviewer, grant panel, or partner with binding-thermodynamics training will read the -18 to -19.5 kcal/mol column as an immediate red flag and discount the entire repository, including the parts that are sound.**

But the finding's headline -- an 'empirical ceiling for non-covalent binding' at ~-18 kcal/mol that 6 of 25 candidates 'exceed' -- does not survive three independent checks. (a) THE COUNT IS WRONG. The reviewer lists app.js:394 (-18.2) among the six, but -18.2 > -18.28, so it does not exceed. (b) THE CITED SOURCE SAYS SOMETHING ELSE. I retrieved Delgadillo et al., PLoS ONE 2019;14(2):e0204194 (PMID 30818336, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0204194) -- the paper the reviewer cites for the biotin calibration. Its abstract states 'The high affinity (KD ~ 10-15 M) of biotin for avidin and streptavidin'. At KD = 1e-15 M, dG = -20.46 kcal/mol and ZERO of the 25 candidates exceed it. (c) THE PHYSICS FRAMING IS DOMAIN OVERREACH. I retrieved Kuntz et al., PNAS 1999;96(18):9997-10002 (PMID 10468550, doi 10.1073/pnas.96.18.9997) and the full text: the plateau it reports is '~-15 kcal/mol (i.e., picomolar dissociation constants)', NOT '-18 kcal/mol' as the reviewer's ground_truth states, and the analysis is per-non-hydrogen-atom for SMALL-MOLECULE ligands -- it does not define a ceiling for protein/peptide interfaces. There is no such ceiling: barnase-barstar, a natural non-covalent protein-protein complex, has Kd ~ 1.3e-14 M and dG0 ~ -19 kcal/mol, essentially equal to the platform's most extreme claim. The platform claims 5-45 fM to 7 pM, uniformly, for unoptimized flexible LINEAR 26-47-mers with unspecified disulfides, across six unrelated target classes, with no experimental data. That is the real finding. Correction: Rewrite the finding as an achievability argument, not a ceiling argument. Correct text: 'The stated dG magnitudes are 3-6 kcal/mol outside the range achievable by de novo peptide design. Cao et al. Kuntz et al. (PNAS 1999) place the plateau for tight ligands at ~-15 kcal/mol; 25 of 25 candidates exceed that plateau and 5 approach barnase-barstar (dG0 ~ -19 kcal/mol), the tightest natural protein-protein complex known.' DELETE the sentence 'Six of the 25 candidates are therefore claimed to bind more tightly than biotin-streptavidin' and delete the Delgadillo citation from this finding's ground_truth, or re-cite it accurately as reporting KD ~ 1e-15 M. Keep the Cao and Kuntz citations, which I verified.

  `clm_794767aa2f5699b2` claimed by `study-peptide-interface`, refuted by `study-candidate-screen`
  - rationale: RETRACTED by study #12 (interface-null-positive-control-v1, prespec 69a5009d6f62, registered 2026-08-22T06:43:11Z before any permutation was folded). The clause 'a low score here is evidence about the candidate rather than about the method' does not hold. #12 folded the same 16 deposited X-ray peptide-receptor complexes -- every one an established binder -- against ten uniform random permutations of each peptide under #7's single-sequence settings, and only 4 of 16 scored above all ten permutations of themselves, against a threshold of 5 registered in advance (H2 FALSIFIED; Bin(16,1/11) expectation 1.45, P(X>=4) = 0.0511). Losing this comparison is what most demonstrated binders do on this instrument, so a low score is not evidence about the candidate in the sense claimed. What survives: #7 did recover 7 of 8 memorisable interfaces, and #12 confirmed the aggregate form (+0.0895 ipTM native minus permutation, Holm p = 0.0148, 13 of 16 differences positive), which licenses a verdict on a batch of pairs and none on any single pair.
  - refuting claim: RETRACTION. Two earlier ledger claims -- clm_382ac4400a7b562c (study-candidate-screen) and clm_794767aa2f5699b2 (study-peptide-interface) -- read study #7's open gate as licensing 'a low score here is evidence about the candidate rather than about the method'. Study #12, interface-null-positive-control-v1, falsified that reading: 16 deposited X-ray complexes, all established binders, each folded against ten uniform random permutations of its own peptide under #7's settings, and only 4 of 16 beat all ten of their own permutations against a pre-registered threshold of 5 (H2 FALSIFIED, P(X>=4) = 0.0511 under Bin(16, 1/11)). Losing the composition-matched comparison is therefore the normal behaviour of a demonstrated binder on this instrument, and a low score in #9 is not evidence about the candidate in the way those claims asserted. The per-candidate reading of the composition-matched null is withdrawn. #7's 7-of-8 recovery and #12's aggregate separation (+0.0895 ipTM, Holm p = 0.0148, 13 of 16 positive) both stand, and license a verdict on a batch of native-versus-shuffle pairs only. Corrected in README.md (Slate #7 gate paragraph), platform/studies/candidate_screen.py and data/study_candidate_screen.json analysis.interpretation_key.
